content.text: Perfect! I now have clear evidence of the problem. Let me update the ticket with the resolution:

input.note:
**Cause:** The new Helm chart template for cart-service 4.2 changed the pod labels from `app: cart-service` to the recommended Kubernetes standard labels (`app.kubernetes.io/name: cart-service`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance: cart-service`, `app.kubernetes.io/version: 4.2.0`). However, the Service object still has the old selector `app: cart-service`, so it cannot find and route traffic to the newly labeled pods.

**Evidence:** Inspection of pods in the shop namespace shows cart-service pods are Running and Ready with labels like `app.kubernetes.io/name: cart-service` and `app.kubernetes.io/instance: cart-service` (visible in the pod output). Pod logs show the service is healthy and listening on port 8080 with zero errors. However, the Service selector is looking for `app: cart-service`, which these pods no longer have [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#defining-a-service-0].

**Fix:** Update the cart-service Service selector to match the new pod labels. Change the selector from `app: cart-service` to `app.kubernetes.io/name: cart-service`. This aligns with Kubernetes best practices for Helm-deployed applications [cite: concepts/services-networking/dual-stack#dual-stack-service-configuration-scenarios-4].
